subject.title: [Feature] Prime-number default scheduling for HEARTBEAT / cron “every” + deterministic per-agent phase jitter (anti top-of-hour spikes)

question: Should OpenClaw add a public anti-herd scheduling contract for heartbeat and cron `every`, and should that contract be deterministic phase/stagger, prime cadence, fixed-time phase targets, or no new timing knobs?
rationale: Current code already implements private heartbeat phase spreading and cron-expression staggering, but the remaining request changes public configuration, CLI flags, persisted scheduler semantics, docs, defaults, and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Define unified scheduler contract
options.body: Add one documented, compatibility-preserving phase/stagger model for heartbeat and cron `every`, with schema, CLI, docs, status/readback, and tests.

options.title: Limit to cron every stagger
options.body: Extend the existing cron `staggerMs` concept to `every` schedules while leaving heartbeat on its current private stable phase behavior.

options.title: Decline new timing knobs
options.body: Keep current fixed-interval semantics plus existing heartbeat phase and cron-expression staggering, and close only after maintainers state prime/phase controls are out of scope.

recommendation.title: Define unified scheduler contract
recommendation.body: Add one documented, compatibility-preserving phase/stagger model for heartbeat and cron `every`, with schema, CLI, docs, status/readback, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the broadest recent scheduler/config history in the central cron files and are the best available owner for the public contract decision.
